messages:

To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2025-08-19T09:16:00-07:00
Subject: Risk: Evaluation pacing slipping against Aug 29 close

Evelyn / Laura —

Quick heads-up: our internal stakeholders ran the last validation sprint yesterday and they flagged two items that will delay the feature validation work by ~7–10 business days: (1) extra environment hardening for limited data sets and (2) an expanded subset of regression tests for our L2 integrator team. Procurement also needs one more pass at the PO terms (cc'd).

We want to stay aligned, but at the current pace we will miss the Aug 29 close. Can you share what flexibility you have for staged acceptance (so we can ship the initial eval gate next week and complete the remaining items in a follow-on acceptance window)? If you have a suggested re-baseline of milestones, please send it over.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Ruiz
Head of Integrations, Acme Corporation

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Risk: Evaluation pacing slipping against Aug 29 close

Alex — thank you for the heads-up and for the report. Appreciate the detail; that helps a lot.

Short answer: we can support a stair-step acceptance approach so you can complete a controlled rollout and still hit an initial production handoff sooner. Proposed minimal change to the MAP (attached):
- Week 1 (Aug 25–29): "Eval Gate 1" — core inference path validated (latency, throughput, basic prompts).
- Week 2 (Sep 1–5): "Eval Gate 2" — integrator regression tests and data-set hardening items.
- Week 3 (Sep 8–12): "Final Acceptance" — full runbook and SLA sign-off.

Operational notes:
- We'll open a dedicated support channel and allocate a small Dedicated pool for two weeks to avoid test throttling.
- If you need a formal credit / SLA adjustment for the extended validation window, propose that now and I will escalate to finance.

I attached v3 of the MAP (stair-step) and a quick risk log with the two items you called out. Laura: can you confirm capacity for the dedicated pool (2x p3-equivalents) and an ops on-call for 8/25–9/12?

Alex — if that runway looks acceptable I can loop Ben for pricing/credits and get Procurement a clean PO addendum.

Best —
Evelyn Hart
Senior Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: "MAP_v3_stair-step.xlsx", "risk_log_q3.csv"

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-20T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: proposed credit / runway for ACME — need decision

Laura / Ben — following up internally. Summary of the public thread: Acme's evaluation work is slipping ~7–10 business days due to environment hardening and integrator regression scope. I proposed a 3-step acceptance MAP (Eval Gate 1/2/Final) which gives them an earlier handoff while completing remaining items in a follow-on window.

Risk profile (short):
- Business: potential close slip of >10 business days if we require single final acceptance.
- Revenue: ACME is Q3 commit; a delay pushes recognition into Q4 (impacts quarter plan).
- Operational: extra Dedicated capacity and a two-week on-call increases variable cost ~5–7K.

Options:
A) Approve stair-step MAP as-is. Offer a one-time operational credit of $6,000 and absorb Dedicated pool cost for 2 weeks.
B) Approve stair-step MAP but request Acme sign an addendum with new Final Acceptance date (Sep 12) and no credit.
C) Hold current date (Aug 29), decline staged acceptance — risk losing ACME as they prefer staggered delivery.

My recommendation: Option A. It preserves the ACME relationship and keeps the momentum while limiting downside. If you approve, I'll reply to Alex and cc Procurement with the MAP final and the PO addendum language.

Ben — if you agree, please confirm the credit lane and let me know if finance needs a short memo; if yes I will draft. Laura — confirm dedicated pool allocation (2x p3-equivalent) and ops on-call schedule.

Evelyn

Subject: Re: Revised MAP: staggered acceptance and close-date runway

Evelyn / team — thanks, that structure looks good and is pragmatic. We accept the stair-step MAP. A couple of small asks before we sign the addendum: (1) can you confirm the expected cutover test window for Eval Gate 1 (we want a 48-hour window with real traffic) and (2) please include a short rollback plan in the MAP so our integrator can sign off.

On the credit: ACME Procurement prefers Option B (no credit) if Redwood will guarantee the Dedicated pool capacity and the 48-hour cutover window control. We can sign the addendum with Final Acceptance Sept 12.

We'll await your PO addendum and the updated MAP with rollback notes.

Best — Alex
